title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 1986 Grothendieck is drafting a combinatorial foundation for 'analysis situs', in the spirit of the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse d'un programme. A 'figure' F is a space |F| (the support; the transcription writes 'sup F', probably 'supp F') built from elementary figures. These are closed strata X_i ⊂ |F|, each with an 'open stratum' int(X_i) = X_i minus its boundary. On p.4: Σ_F is the set of strata of F. Σ'_F, the set of elementary sub-figures, is identified with a down-closed ('fermée') subset of the poset F_él of elementary figures ordered by inclusion. Inclusion of figures then becomes inclusion of these closed subsets.

This page opens with a crossed-out attempt to characterise which subsets Φ ⊂ F_él are of the form Σ'_F. The criterion would be (a) Φ closed in the poset, plus (b) a condition on the families of supports |φ|. It was abandoned unfinished.

He then defines a subset A ⊂ |F| to be F-saturated if it is saturated for the equivalence relation whose classes are the open strata int(X_i), i.e. A is a union of open strata. The margin notes the expected stability properties: saturation is preserved by ∩, ∪ and inverse images f^{-1}(A). It also notes the compatibility for a sub-figure F' ⊂ F: for A ⊂ |F'|, A is F'-saturated iff it is F-saturated.

Next he sets up a compatibility condition for two figures F, F' (presumably sub-figures of a common ambient, or figures in a common space). The first version, crossed out, was '|F|∩|F'| is F- and F'-saturated'. The retained version is:
(a) for all strata X ∈ Σ_F and X' ∈ Σ_F', X∩X' is F_X-saturated and F'_{X'}-saturated, where F_X is the figure generated by X.

On p.6 this is shown equivalent to:
(b) any connected open strata U_i of F and U'_j of F' are either disjoint or equal.

Proof of (a)⇒(b): take x ∈ U_i∩U'_j. Then X_i∩X'_j is closed, F_{X_i}-saturated, and meets the dense open stratum U_i, so it contains X_i. By symmetry X_i = X'_j. Equality of the open strata then follows by induction on max(dim F, dim F'), reducing to the boundary figures.

Purpose: this is the condition that two stratified figures are 'compatible', i.e. that F ∪ F' and F ∩ F' are again figures. This is the analogue of two subcomplexes of a common CW or polyhedral complex.
errors: The step from X_i = X'_j to U_i = U'_j needs the open stratum to be intrinsically determined by the closed stratum. Equivalently, ∂X_i computed in F must equal ∂X'_j computed in F'. This is not automatic from the definitions on the page; Grothendieck himself defers it to an induction on dimension on p.6, which is only sketched.
The argument also silently uses that int(X_i) is dense in X_i and connected (the X_i are closures of connected open strata). This is part of the implicit axioms on elementary figures.
The opening characterisation of the subsets Φ of the form Σ'_F is abandoned; condition (b) is never stated.

ideas.what: Elementary figures form a poset; a figure is a down-closed subset, and inclusion of figures is inclusion of these subsets
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of a regular CW / polyhedral complex; subcomplexes as down-sets (Alexandrov topology)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) only sketches tame topology programmatically

ideas.what: F-saturated subsets = unions of open strata; stable under ∩, ∪ and inverse image
ideas.modern_name: Constructible / stratum-saturated subsets of a stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical in stratification theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather; o-minimal cell decompositions)

ideas.what: Compatibility of two figures: open strata pairwise disjoint or equal, equivalent to the stratum-wise saturation condition
ideas.modern_name: Compatible stratifications / subcomplexes of a common complex

deep.surprise_reason: This is foundational bookkeeping for a stratified, 'tame' combinatorial topology: saturated sets and compatibility of figures. It is standard in substance (subcomplexes, compatible stratifications). The archival interest lies only in documenting how Grothendieck set up his 1986 analysis situs, not in new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'une partie Φ de F' and 'partie fermée de T' should read 'partie Φ de F_él' and 'partie fermée de F_él', matching p.4.
'|F| = sup F' is likely '|F| = supp F' (the support of F).
'des An. Hom' is doubtful; the sense is 'réunion de strates ouvertes int(X_i)', likely 'des X_i' or similar.
Garbled sentence: 'La signification géométrique … réunion de strates (géométriques)' probably says that saturation means being a union of geometric strata.
